```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 0.3)

# draws n full-width blank lines (margin to margin) for handwritten answers,
# as a single plot so spacing is deterministic; pair with fig.height = 0.3 * n
blank_lines <- function(n = 1) {
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
  plot(NA, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, n), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    segments(0, n - i + 0.5, 1, n - i + 0.5, lwd = 1)
  }
}

# reserves blank work space (no ruled lines) for equation manipulation /
# show-your-work; pair with fig.height set to however much room is needed
blank_space <- function() {
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
  plot.new()
}
```

```{r key-helpers, include=FALSE}
ans_col <- rgb(200, 0, 130, maxColorValue = 255)
# redraws blank_table() so cells flagged TRUE in `ans` use the answer color
blank_table <- function(headers, body, col_widths = NULL,
                        header_height = 0.35, row_height = 0.5,
                        cex = 0.95, bold_rows = integer(0), ans = NULL) {
  nc <- length(headers); nr <- length(body)
  if (is.null(col_widths)) col_widths <- rep(1, nc)
  col_widths <- col_widths / sum(col_widths)
  cx <- c(0, cumsum(col_widths))
  h_total <- header_height + nr * row_height
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0), family = "serif")
  plot(NA, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, h_total), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "",
       xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i")
  y <- h_total
  segments(0, y, 1, y, lwd = 1.5)
  y <- y - header_height
  segments(0, y, 1, y, lwd = 1.5)
  for (i in seq_len(nr)) {
    y <- y - row_height
    segments(0, y, 1, y, lwd = if (i == nr) 1.5 else 0.5,
             col = if (i == nr) "black" else "grey70")
  }
  for (v in cx) segments(v, 0, v, h_total, lwd = 1)
  yh <- h_total - header_height / 2
  for (j in seq_len(nc)) text((cx[j] + cx[j + 1]) / 2, yh, labels = headers[[j]], font = 2, cex = cex)
  y <- h_total - header_height
  for (i in seq_len(nr)) {
    yc <- y - row_height / 2
    for (j in seq_len(nc)) {
      val <- body[[i]][[j]]
      is_ans <- !is.null(ans) && isTRUE(ans[[i]][[j]])
      if (!identical(val, "")) text((cx[j] + cx[j + 1]) / 2, yc, labels = val, cex = cex,
                                    font = if (i %in% bold_rows) 2 else 1,
                                    col = if (is_ans) ans_col else "black")
    }
    y <- y - row_height
  }
}
```

\ans{\textbf{Answer key.} Answers are in magenta.}


**NRES 746 -- Week 2, Lecture 2: Limits and a Derivative**

&nbsp;


&nbsp;

**Instructions:** Work alone for about 5 minutes. Then compare with a
neighbor.

## Part 1: What happens at the edges?

For each function below, use the "throw out the lower-order terms"
trick to state what happens as $x\to0$ and as
$x\to\infty$. You don't need to show work, just the two limiting
behaviors. We've already done the first two together in class!

**1a.** Michaelis-Menten: $f(x) = \dfrac{ax}{b+x}$

As $x\to0$: \ans{$\approx (a/b)\,x \to 0$} &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; As $x\to\infty$: \ans{$\to a$}

**1b.** Ricker: $f(x) = ax\,e^{-bx}$

As $x\to0$: \ans{$\approx a x \to 0$} &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; As $x\to\infty$: \ans{$\to 0$}

**1c.** Logistic: $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{1+e^{-bx}}$

As $x\to0$: \ans{$\to 1/2$} &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; As $x\to\infty$: \ans{$\to 1$}

**1d.** Holling type III: $f(x) = \dfrac{ax^2}{b^2+x^2}$

As $x\to0$: \ans{$\approx (a/b^2)\,x^2 \to 0$} &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; As $x\to\infty$: \ans{$\to a$}

## Part 2: What kind of point is $x=0$?

The logistic function, $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{1+e^{-bx}}$, is the simplest
sigmoid in the bestiary. It is symmetric around $x=0$.

**2a.** Qualitatively, how would you characterize the derivative of the logistic function at x=0 relative to 
the derivative of this function at all other inputs (x)? 

\ans{It's the steepest point: the derivative is largest at $x = 0$ and shrinks toward 0 in both directions.}

**2b.** In Lab 1 you found that the Ricker function's derivative is
zero at its peak. This makes it a 'critical point'. Is $f'(0)$ also zero at
the logistic's midpoint (x=0)? If not, what kind of special point is $x=0$
instead? (Hint: think about the curve's concavity just before and
just after $x=0$ -- what would that imply about the *second*
derivative at $x=0$?)

\ans{No: $f'(0) = b/4 > 0$. It's an inflection point. The curve is concave up before 0 and concave down after, so $f''(0) = 0$.}


**Optional, for fun!** Rewrite the logistic function $f(x)$ as $(1+e^{-bx})^{-1}$, then find $f'(x)$ using
the chain rule (twice: once for the outer power, once for the inner
exponential).

*Reminders:* $\dfrac{d}{dx}\,u^n = n\,u^{n-1}\,u'$ &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; $\dfrac{d}{dx}\,e^{g(x)} = g'(x)\,e^{g(x)}$

Show your work:

\ansbegin

$$f'(x) = -1\,(1+e^{-bx})^{-2}\cdot(-b\,e^{-bx}) = \frac{b\,e^{-bx}}{(1+e^{-bx})^2}$$

\ansend

Now evaluate $f'(x)$ at $x=0$.

$f'(0) =$ \ans{$\dfrac{b \cdot 1}{(1+1)^2} = b/4$}
